source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text:
Durian can be planted using two methods: the pit-digging method (suited to sites with an accessible water source and shallower water table) and the no-pit / mound method (suited to sites where the water table lies deep underground).

For the pit method: mark out planting rows and spacing first, with the standard spacing being 9 meters between trees each way, giving about 20 trees per hectare (spacing may be adjusted based on soil fertility). Dig the planting hole, keeping the topsoil (humus-rich soil dug from the top layer) separate from the subsoil. Line the bottom and mix in compost or well-rotted manure (about 5kg per hole) plus topsoil back into the hole around the young tree's root ball. Set the potted seedling into the hole so that the top of the root ball sits level with or very slightly above the surrounding ground, backfill, and firm the soil around the base without compacting it too hard. Stake the young tree with a strong stake tied loosely enough not to girdle the trunk as it grows, to protect it against wind while it establishes. Water immediately after planting and mulch around the base with straw or dried grass, leaving a small gap right around the trunk itself so the mulch does not trap moisture against the bark and invite collar rot.
